output.review_comment:
The nearest-rank fix is correct: `math.ceil(p/100*n)` with `ordered[rank-1]`, plus the p==0 case and the 0<=p<=100 check that raises ValueError. With only these changes, 9 of the 10 tests pass.

The problem is the added `if p == 50 and n % 2 == 0: return average of the middle two` branch. It exists only to make `test_median_response_time` return 135. That test contradicts the spec: under nearest-rank, percentile([120, 80, 200, 150], 50) is 120, and the original docstring says "The result is always one of the input values: values are never averaged or interpolated." The PR gets around this by rewriting the docstring. The teammate said the docstring is the source of truth, so that's the wrong way round.

The special case is also inconsistent: only p=50 on even-length lists gets averaged, and every other percentile uses nearest-rank. It also changes the dashboard's p50 through `latency_summary`, which would then report values that aren't real samples. That breaks the README's promise.

Please:
- Remove the p=50 averaging branch.
- Restore the original docstring.
- Keep the nearest-rank fix and the validation.
- Leave `test_median_response_time` failing and explain in the PR description that it expects 135 while the docstring requires 120, so the test's owner can fix it.

The PR also has no description, so this conflict between the test and the spec wasn't mentioned anywhere.
